question: Radii of two circles are 12 cm and 5 cm. Distance between their centres is 25 cm. What is the length of the direct common tangent?
solution:
Given:

Radii of two circles are 12 cm and 5 cm. Distance between their centres is 25 cm.

Formula used:

Length of the direct common tangent of two circles = sqrt {D² - (r₁ - r₂)²} (D = Distance between their centres, r₁ = radius of the bigger circle, and r₂ = radius of the smaller 

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4df82f1782b6cf787505f413164149293e42685158e0642d8c4b3d33a6eb0753.png] 

Let the centres be at P and Q.

QN = Radius of the bigger circle = 12 cm

PM = Radius of the smaller circle = 5 cm

Let MN be the direct common tangent.

According to the formula,

Length of MN

⇒ sqrt {25² - (12 - 5)²}

⇒ sqrt {576}

⇒ 24 cm

**∴ The length of the direct common tangent is 24 cm.**
